procedural_history.originating_court: Not explicitly stated, but implied to be a trial court since the High Court heard criminal appeals.
procedural_history.impugned_order: Judgment and order dated April 18, 1966, of the Bombay High Court in Criminal Appeals Nos. 1646, 1631, 1652, 1628 and 1626 of 1963.
procedural_history.high_court_proceedings: All the convicted persons filed appeals in the High Court. During the pendency of the appeal A-11 absconded. The High Court upheld the convictions of A-36 and A-7 but modified their sentences (A-36 released on probation, A-7 fined and given a one-day simple imprisonment). The High Court dismissed the appeals of A-6, 8, 11, 12, 14, 15, 16 and 17.
procedural_history.supreme_court_posture: A-6, 8, 12, 14, 15, and 16 appealed to the Supreme Court after obtaining special leave. The Supreme Court case is comprised of Criminal Appeals Nos. 139 to 144 of 1966.

decision.appeal_result: Criminal Appeal Nos. 139, 142, 143 and 144 of 1966 are allowed in part and dismissed in other respects. Criminal Appeals Nos. 140 and 141 of 1966 are allowed.
decision.conviction_status: Maganlal Naranji Patel and N. B. Mukherjee are acquitted of all the charges. Convictions of appellants in the other appeals are upheld.

directions: All the sentences passed on the appellants [in Criminal Appeals Nos. 139, 142, 143 and 144 of 1966] will run concurrently.

issue.issue_text: did he wrongly refuse to recall PW 50 Ali for cross-examination?

facts: Witness PW 50 Ali's examination-in-chief was completed on October 10, 1960, and his cross-examination was completed on September 4, 1961.
Months later, on March 6, 1962, and again on June 21, 1962, the defense applied to recall Ali for further cross-examination.
The defense claimed that Ali was repentant and wanted to state that he had previously given false evidence.
law: A court has the inherent power to recall a witness if it is satisfied that the witness is prepared to give evidence that is materially different from what they had given at the trial.
application: The Supreme Court found that the defense had not provided any grounds to justify recalling the witness.
Specifically, the defense failed to produce an affidavit from Ali or any other material evidence to show that his original testimony was incorrect or that he was prepared to give different evidence.
Without any material upon which the court could be satisfied that the witness would change his testimony, the condition for exercising the power to recall was not met.
reasoning.conclusion: The Supreme Court concluded that the magistrate had rightly disallowed the applications to recall PW 50 Ali because no proper grounds were made out for doing so.

arguments.issue_text: did he wrongly refuse to recall PW 50 Ali for cross-examination?
appellant_arguments: The appellant (Kochra) was prejudiced by the rejection of the application to recall the witness (Yusuf).
The appellant wanted to recall the witness to establish through cross-examination that he had sent the cables Z-745 from Beirut.
respondent_arguments: The learned Magistrate rightly disallowed the prayer for recalling Ali.
A court can recall a witness if it is satisfied that he is prepared to give evidence which is materially different from what he had given at the trial.
In this case, there was no material upon which the Court could be so satisfied.

ratio_decidendi.ratio: A fraudulent evasion of the restriction imposed by s. 8(1) of the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act 1947 is punishable under s. 167(81) of the Sea Customs Act, 1878. The Supreme Court will not normally re-appraise evidence when there are concurrent findings of fact by lower courts, unless the findings are perverse, vitiated by an error of law, or have resulted in a grave miscarriage of justice.
obiter: It is not necessary to express an opinion on whether the Indian Aircraft Rules, 1920 could authorize the levy of a tax or create a new offence punishable under s. 167(81) of the Sea Customs Act, 1878.

judicial_reasoning.core_finding: The Court found that the application to recall the witness was not made in good faith and was, for this reason alone, liable to be rejected.
legal_tests_applied: Whether an application to recall a witness is made in good faith.
why_appellant_lost: The appellant's application to recall the witness was found to have not been made in good faith.
why_respondent_won: The court determined that the application was liable to be rejected on the sole ground that it was not made in good faith.
